Ear Drama · R3f · proposal for the owner · 2026-11-23

Library, organized

Three ways to rebuild Library on every platform, with a recommendation. Nothing in the app has changed; you choose.

"the library tab on all of the apps has become a kichen sink aproach to putting everything into an undesigned list of items. ... Continue, Queue, and Following all seem to be the same thing and empty fields don't do anything for a user except to make them scroll through more material before they get to what they want to use" (you, 2026-11-23)

Kept from your earlier ruling: Library stays the app's settings home, with no Settings page (2026-11-22), and listening and making get equal weight (2026-11-16).

What Library is today

Three stores, one questionContinue = episodes started and not finished. Queue = the order you built. Following = shows you bookmarked; it never produces an episode. All three answer "what do I listen to next?", and Continue also repeats Home's Continue.
Empty sections are kept by ruleiOS, tvOS and Android design docs say every section keeps its header and a caption. A new listener on iOS scrolls past six headers and six captions before Account.
Voices takes overWeb in a Mac browser: about 80% of Library's height is the device voice list. On the Pixel 8a, Voices is the first thing on screen, above Continue.
Making is a flat dumpOn the Pixel, Ear dramas is ten rows, nine of them "The Albany Depot", with nothing to tell them apart. It also repeats Record's Yours.
History is heavyApple and Android draw up to 100 finished episodes inline, above everything you make and every preference.
No common orderExport, Listen together, the site pages and Voices sit in different places on each platform. The web hides everything behind five tabs.

Not captured: iPhone Duo, iPad, Mac, Apple TV and the TVs. Apple and tvOS were audited from the code.

What carries over: merge "what's next" into one list where each row says why it is there, with your own order before anything automatic; never draw an empty section as a block; keep preferences out of the collection, here as one compact group of rows at the foot; treat history as a drawer, not the page.

Three directions

All three share the same foot: Account (Sign in / Synced), Voices (with its current state; opens Library's own Voices place, no longer drawn in full), Listen together, Export my data, About Ear Drama (credits, privacy, take-down, delete an account). A TV shows Account, Show a Reading and About.

A. Up next, Made by you, then the back pages Recommended

One page, no tabs. Each section appears only when it has something, in this order: Up next (started episodes with their progress, then your queue in your order, then one "Next in {show}" row per show you follow, by a stated rule; five rows, then All), Made by you (productions grouped by play, then Your parts and each class as one line), Shows you follow (the shelf), History and Downloads as one line each, then the foot.

ForAnswers both of your points directly; making gets its own named section, not a tab or a dump; following finally does something, without a feed. A designer could redraw it from one paragraph.
AgainstThe "next episode of a followed show" rule needs an order per show (air date, else log number). Home's Continue would repeat Up next's first rows.

B. Listening | Making

A two-way switch at the top. Listening: Up next (started, then queued), Shows you follow, History and Downloads lines. Making: Waiting on you (parts someone's production needs from you), Productions grouped by play, Marks, Classes. The foot under either.

ForThe plainest statement of listen and make; a maker never scrolls past listening.
AgainstA switch inside a tab hides half your things (the same fault as today's five web tabs, gentler). Following stays its own thing rather than merging.

C. One timeline

A Resume card, then your Queued episodes, then Recent: everything you did, newest first, grouped by day, each row tagged Heard, Finished, Recorded, Followed or Queued.

ForNothing to learn; listening and making interleave as they happened.
AgainstTo find a production you scroll past what you heard; followed shows only exist on the day you followed them; the same episode can appear twice. It is a history with a resume button, and history was the rarest need in the audit.

What moves under A

  • Removed: every empty section's header and caption; the web's five tabs; Voices drawn in full on Library; Classes' always-drawn Make and Join buttons in Library.
  • Moved: Continue and Queue into Up next; Following into the shelf and Up next; History and Downloads to one line each; Account, Voices, Listen together, Export and the site pages into one foot group, in the same order on every platform (Android moves Voices from the top to the foot).
  • New: productions grouped by play; Your parts in Library when something waits; a published "next episode of a show you follow" rule.
  • Per platform: web one scroll of sections; iOS and Mac a List with an inset-grouped foot, Voices pushed in Library's stack; iPad and wide web two columns; Android the same order in a LazyColumn; TVs as focus shelves with Account, Show a Reading and About.

Questions for you

  1. Followed shows in Up next. Should each followed show add one "Next in {show}" row, or should following stay only as the shelf?
  2. Voices as its own place under Library. Is a Voices page opened from Library's foot acceptable under "no Settings page", or should it open in place on Library?
  3. Home's Continue. Keep it, shorten it to the last episode you were playing, or drop it now that Library leads with Up next?
  4. Made by you and Record's Yours. Library holds everything you made and Record keeps only the unfinished, or one points to the other?
  5. Making and joining classes. Move Make a class and Join a class to Record and the class page, or keep a Classes line in Library?
  6. The foot's heading. "Account and preferences", "You", or none?
  7. Up next's length. Five rows then All, or every row?
